title: Loose pieces: what can be taken for free?
outcomes: Names the loose pieces of either side
Takes a loose piece, the one with the higher counting value first
Checks for a far-away defender before calling a piece free
Says when there is nothing to take

steps.text: A piece is **loose** when an enemy piece attacks it and none of its own side defends it: the enemy can take it for free. Related words: **undefended** means no friendly piece guards it, even if nobody attacks it yet; **hanging** (*en prise*) means attacked without enough defence; **tactically vulnerable** means defended but still losable to a trick or exchange. Two habits stop most beginner losses. Look at their pieces for loose ones. Then look at your own, after every move your opponent makes.

steps.caption: White to move. Which black piece is loose?

line.say: The rook takes the knight. No black piece defends d5, so nothing recaptures.
Black has lost a whole knight for nothing.

claims.statement: Only the knight on d5 is loose.

steps.text:
A loose piece is free only on conditions.
**Count every defender**, including pieces that guard from far away along a file or diagonal.
**Ask what the capture costs.** A piece that has a defender is not free: if the defender can recapture, you may lose more than you win.

steps.title: Same attack, one change
steps.prompt: Only the position of White's rook changes.
When you decided a piece was free, what did you check first? Did you ever miss a defender that stood far away?
